title: architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-rfc-142.json
content:
Architecture Review Meeting Notes — RFC-142: KV Cache Sharding and Hotspot Mitigation

Date: 2026-02-25
Time: 10:00–11:00 PT
Location: Zoom + #eng-serving-runtime
Owner: Asha Menon
Attendees: Asha Menon, Daniel Park, Priya Shah, Mark Liu, Elena Gomez, Ravi Patel, Sophie Chen

Purpose
- Review RFC-142 and decide on the design direction to shard the KV cache to mitigate hotspots and reduce tail latency for long-context workloads.
- Align on rollout plan, metrics, and next steps for implementation and testing.

Agenda
1) Quick recap of problem & goals (Asha)
2) Proposal walkthrough (Priya)
3) Alternatives discussed and tradeoffs (Mark)
4) Operational concerns: metrics/tracing, rollout, compatibility (Daniel, Elena)
5) Decision and action items

Recap of problem- Long-context workloads (document summarization, retrieval-augmented generation) cause heavy reuse of KV cache prefixes and create GPU-local hotspots.- Observed issues: increased P95/P99 token latency, uneven memory utilization across GPU pool, degraded throughput for co-located tenants under bursty prefixes.- Goals: reduce tail latency, balance memory/compute across GPUs, maintain correctness of autoregressive generation and compatibility with batching and cache re-use.

Proposal summary (RFC-142)- Shard KV cache across GPUs using a prefix-based consistent hashing scheme. Prefix = first N tokens after user prompt boundary (configurable; default N=8).- Each shard maintains its own LRU-based eviction and per-shard memory accounting.
- Router: map incoming request to a primary shard based on prefix hash. If shard unavailable or overloaded, fallback to: (1) route to replica shard, or (2) serve from a compatible smaller model variant (fallback policy controlled by route config).
- Cross-shard requests: for batched requests that span shards, runtime performs lightweight coordination to fetch per-shard KV slices; optimization to avoid copying full KV when possible (reference semantics).
- Metrics/tags: cache.shard_id, cache.hit, cache.miss, cache.eviction_reason, cache.request_type (inference|replay), cache.prefix_hash.

Alternatives considered (and why rejected)
- Centralized KV service: single RPC cache layer outside GPUs. Pros: global view. Cons: added network hop increases token latency; central point of failure; worse for high-throughput low-latency paths. Rejected for production path due to latency and reliability concerns.
- Full-state transfer per-request: move full KV state between GPUs for every request to ensure locality. Pros: correctness. Cons: excessive PCIe/NVLink transfer, kills throughput. Rejected.
- Global eviction policy (single LRU across pool): complex coordination, high metadata churn; still susceptible to hotspot writes. Rejected.

Key design decisions (agreed by attendees)
1) Sharding approach: adopt prefix-based consistent hashing (RFC-142) with configurable prefix-length. Rationale: good balance of locality and distribution for typical workloads.
2) Eviction policy: LRU-within-shard + size-aware eviction. Keep per-shard watermarks and allow the router to mark a shard as ‘hot’ when memory pressure crosses threshold.
3) Fallback policy: prefer replica shard routing first; if replica mix unavailable, fallback to smaller model variant (configurable per-customer route).
4) API/backwards compatibility: no client-visible API changes. Cache behavior controlled by deployment config and feature flags; keep old path as default for a canary period.
5) Rollout: staged canary (see rollout plan).

Operational considerations- Metrics & observability: need per-shard dashboards (cache hit/miss, evictions, memory utilization, token latency p50/p95/p99). Daniel to add metric names and propose Grafana dashboard layout.
- Tracing: instrument request flow with shard_id, prefix_hash and KV fetch duration. Elena to add tracing spans and update tracing playbook.
- Telemetry limits: ensure added metrics are high-cardinality-aware; shard_id is bounded by pool size.
- Feature flags: gate sharded cache behind a runtime feature flag + route-level override. Sophie to implement flag scaffolding.
- Compatibility with batching: router must coalesce requests by target shard to avoid cross-shard synchronous fetches where possible.

Rollout plan (agreed)
1) Prototype + unit tests in branch (2 weeks) — Asha/Mark
2) Internal canary on Dedicated small pool (one region) for synthetic load (1 week). Monitor P95/P99 latencies, cache hit rate per-shard.
3) Gradual ramp to non-critical hosted API routes (2–3 weeks) with feature flag and traffic percentage controls.
4) Full rollout to hosted API + Dedicated after 4 weeks of stable metrics.
5) Private deployments: provide config and docs; leave disabled by default for customers to opt in.

Success metrics (primary)
- 20–40% reduction in P95 token latency for hotspot workloads in canary
- No >5% regression in overall throughput for co-located tenants
- Cache hit rate improvement or stable hit rate with lower tail latency
- No increase in error rate or out-of-memory incidents in canary

Implementation notes / constraints- Memory accounting must be precise to avoid cross-shard double-alloc. Use existing memory tracker code paths where possible.
- Keep data structures quantization-friendly (no new fp32-heavy metadata per-token).
- Ensure rollout does not change single-request semantics (determinism for generation).

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups)
- Optimal prefix length: default 8 is a heuristic. Need simulation over production prefix distribution. Action: Mark to run simulation and recommend prefix_len by 2026-03-05.
- Replica placement strategy: how many replicas per shard for redundancy vs costs? Need cost model. Action: Priya + Ravi to propose replica counts and cost tradeoffs by 2026-03-08.
- Cross-shard batch coordination algorithm: two-phase fetch vs opportunistic coalesce. Implementation tradeoffs required. Action: Daniel to prototype coordination shim and compare latencies by 2026-03-10.

Action items
- Asha Menon: lead prototype implementation + integration tests. Target branch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987. Due: 2026-03-10.
- Daniel Park: add shard-level metrics, Grafana dashboard proposal, and tracing spans. Create ticket JIRA-ENG-1252. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Priya Shah + Ravi Patel: produce replica placement and cost analysis for different pool sizes. Linked doc: Confluence RFC-142/replicas. Due: 2026-03-08.
- Mark Liu: run prefix-distribution simulation on sampling of production traces and recommend prefix_len. Report in JIRA-ENG-1254. Due: 2026-03-05.
- Elena Gomez: update tracing playbook, add spans for KV fetch and shard routing. Due: 2026-03-09.
- Sophie Chen: implement runtime feature flag + route override for sharded cache. PR and tests. Due: 2026-03-12.
- QA (TBD): prepare synthetic hotspot test harness and run canary tests during dedicated canary window. Schedule test window after prototype landed.

Follow-up-
Next sync: lightweight checkpoint on 2026-03-04 (15 min) to confirm prototype timeline and any blockers.
- Full design review and canary readiness check on 2026-03-11.

Notes / misc-
Referenced artifacts: RFC-142 full doc (Confluence), GH PR #987 (implementation branch), Jira tickets JIRA-ENG-1248 (parent task), JIRA-ENG-1252/1254 (metrics/sim).
- Meeting recorded: internal Zoom recording (link posted in meeting thread).

Decision summary (short): Proceed with prefix-based consistent hashing sharding with LRU-per-shard and replica-first fallback. Gate behind runtime feature flag; roll out via canary on Dedicated, then to hosted routes.

Document history-
- 2026-02-25: Draft notes captured during review (Asha)
- 2026-02-26: Minor edits to action items, added links and deadlines (Asha)
